title: Fine-grain emission probes for token cost reconciliation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: produce per-token emission probes that let downstream billing/analytics correlate CPU/GPU time and token unit cost with cache behavior and batching decisions.

Scope: instrument the runtime to emit an ordered series of lightweight events per request that capture:
- token_index (0-based), token_phase (decode/emit/kv-lookup), timestamp_ns, cpu_ns_delta, gpu_ns_delta (when available), cache_hit: true|false, batch_id, model_variant, request_id, route_tag.

Non-goals: full payload of token text, user PII, or storing every event long-term. We will not change billing semantics in this change — this is telemetry only.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Event granularity: emit per-token probes only at the emission boundary and on KV cache lookup completion to avoid doubling probe volume. Emitting both 'emit' and 'kv-lookup' phases per token captures cache impact without instrumenting every internal op.
- Sampling policy: default 1% sampling on production hosts with deterministic reservoir sampling keyed by request_id to preserve correlation across retries. Test and canary clusters at 100%.
- Payload size vs fidelity: we will avoid embedding token text; instead include token_index and an opaque token_hash for troubleshooting. This keeps events small (~120 bytes).
- Kernel timing availability: GPU timers are available on dedicated pools; for hosted pools we will fall back to cpu_ns_delta + estimated_gpu_ms tag.

Telemetry pipeline changes:
- Traces: add a new span kind `token.emit` with attributes matching the event fields for easy correlation in distributed traces.
- Metrics: derive counters and histograms from events: token_emit_latency_ms (hist), token_kv_lookup_latency_ms (hist), token_cache_hit_rate (counter by true/false), tokens_per_request (hist).
- Logs: low-frequency aggregated log records (one per request) summarizing token-level aggregates for long retention (30d).

Storage and retention:
- Raw per-token events streamed to Kafka topic `telemetry.token_probes` with 7-day retention.
- Aggregation job (Spark/Flink) will produce hourly rollups to Prometheus-compatible metrics backend and long-term aggregated tables in ClickHouse for billing reconciliation.

APIs and schema:
- Event JSON schema version v1: fields described above plus schema_version and service_instance. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Token+Emission+Probes+v1 (draft).

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime emits token probes for 100% of requests in canary and 1% in prod.
- Ingestion pipeline accepts events and produces token_kv_lookup_latency_ms and token_cache_hit_rate metrics within 10 minutes.
- Console dashboard `Token Cost Reconciliation` shows per-model token latency and estimated per-token cost breakdown and highlights requests with unexpected cache deltas.
- End-to-end test that simulates 10k requests with synthetic cache-hit/miss distribution and verifies aggregated metrics match expected within 2%.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge instrumentation behind feature flag `token_probes_v1` (runtime).
2) Deploy to canary cluster at 100% for 3 days; run ingestion pipeline in mirror mode.
3) Gradual ramp to production with 1% sampling. Monitor ingestion lag and downstream storage size.

Observability and dashboards:
- New dashboard `Observability / Token Cost Reconciliation`: panels for token_emit_latency_ms p50/p95/p99 by model, token_cache_hit_rate over time, token_latency_by_cache_hit (histogram split), requests_with_high_cache_delta (>25ms), and top routes by per-token cost.
- Alerts: token_kv_lookup_latency_ms p99 > 100ms for 10m, and ingestion lag > 600s.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests for event serialization and schema validation.
- Integration test harness that runs a small runtime with mocked KV store and asserts emitted events.
- Load test: 20k RPS on canary with sampling 100% to validate pipeline throughput.

Open questions:
- Do we want to include token generation reasons (e.g., finish_reason) on the event? (pm requested but we deferred due to size).
- Should storage retention for aggregated tables be 90d or 365d? Defaulting to 90d for now.
